name: LIFE cross-format linkability scenario matrix
purpose: Require comparable observer capabilities and counterfactuals across credential formats without pretending every channel applies identically to every format.
principles: Declare the observer and its capabilities before collecting scores.
Keep attacker-visible artifacts separate from ground-truth subject labels.
Use the same subject cohort, task, session schedule and auxiliary-data budget across compared formats.
Run each attack separately and also report the strongest observed attack; never average away a successful attack.
Treat inapplicable format-specific channels as not-applicable, not as a privacy success.
Report residual threats and operational leakage separately from cryptographic proof properties.

fixture_strata.stable_artifact: Repeated or cohort-identifying credential artifacts, stable keys or issuer identifiers.
fixture_strata.status_metadata: Status / registry lookups, network timing and operational metadata.
fixture_strata.structure_only: Format-visible proof or presentation structure such as disclosed-message indexes, message count, size or ordering.
fixture_strata.noisy_control: No deliberate identity signal; control for leakage caused by labels, IDs, ordering or dataset generation.

scenarios.sd_jwt: applicable; repeated issuer-signed SD-JWT bytes or stable key material can correlate sessions
scenarios.bbs: profile-dependent; derived proofs should differ, but issuer-key cohort and disclosed metadata remain observable
scenarios.mdoc: profile-dependent; test issuer-authenticated credential and device-binding artifacts separately
scenarios.counterfactual: Compare byte-identical reuse against freshly derived or reissued artifacts while keeping claims and transaction purpose fixed.

scenarios.observer: single verifier with bounded auxiliary data
scenarios.counterfactual: Hold proof mechanics fixed and ablate each revealed field and field combination; evaluate top-1 and top-k re-identification.

scenarios.observer: issuer, status service, verifier or colluding parties
scenarios.sd_jwt: profile-dependent; measure list or endpoint access, not just token contents
scenarios.bbs: profile-dependent; measure status mechanism used by the deployment
scenarios.mdoc: profile-dependent; measure status or revocation mechanism used by the deployment
scenarios.counterfactual: Compare direct online lookups, cached status evidence and privacy-preserving status assertions where supported; record freshness and revocation latency.

scenarios.mdoc: applicable at deployment layer, including proximity/device protocols where in scope
scenarios.counterfactual: Evaluate content-only, size-only, timing-only and joint attacks; keep transport assumptions explicit.

scenarios.sd_jwt: applicable to disclosure shape, claim order, token size and optional disclosure sets
scenarios.bbs: applicable; BBS proof message count and revealed indexes can be linkability signals
scenarios.mdoc: profile-dependent; measure disclosed namespace/item sets, response shape and size
scenarios.counterfactual: Compare a fixed disclosure set across subjects, then vary the set while holding subject labels independent; report the smallest structural cohort.

scenarios.observer: verifier and optionally a colluding issuer
scenarios.bbs: applicable; issuer key partitioning can mark cohorts
scenarios.mdoc: applicable to issuer certificates and trust-chain choice
scenarios.counterfactual: Compare one-key, planned rotation and artificially partitioned-key issuance; report cohort sizes and attacker advantage.

scenarios.observer: issuer or service observing issuance, renewal or limited-use token replenishment
scenarios.counterfactual: Compare online issuance / replenishment with pre-issued batches or privacy-preserving refresh patterns where technically supported.
Run longitudinal traces with identical credential facts but shuffled service order and cadence; evaluate held-out subjects.

scenarios.observer: verifier or colluding verifier with a declared auxiliary dataset
scenarios.counterfactual: Publish auxiliary-data provenance, join keys and coverage; compare no-auxiliary and bounded-auxiliary results without exposing real personal records.
Shuffle scores relative to labels and verify attack advantage returns to chance within uncertainty; test for pair-ID, row-order and split leakage.

scenarios.sd_jwt: applicable; do not claim issuer-verifier unlinkability from SD-JWT alone
scenarios.bbs: profile-dependent; test key partitioning, issuance records and disclosed metadata despite unlinkable derived proofs
scenarios.mdoc: profile-dependent; make trust-ecosystem and issuer visibility assumptions explicit
scenarios.counterfactual: State whether the issuer knows credential presentation events or can correlate issuance, key cohort, status and timing; report the residual channel.

comparison_protocol.subject_split: Train/tune identities and held-out test identities must be disjoint. The evaluator mechanically rejects overlap in the provided identity namespace.
comparison_protocol.same_cohort: Compared formats must use matched subject cohorts, target tasks, purpose, session count, session schedule and auxiliary-data budget.
comparison_protocol.attack_suite: At minimum run a simple rule baseline, a tabular supervised baseline when labels exist, and a longitudinal sequence baseline when trace data exists; report each separately.
comparison_protocol.winner_rule: Do not assign a universal format winner. Report profile-specific results, uncertainty and remaining channels; any claimed privacy improvement must preserve the declared task utility and security requirements.
comparison_protocol.smoke_fixture_note: The checked-in fixture covers only four broad strata and is not a coverage claim for the full scenario catalogue.
